- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- In low sentiment (≤0.3) environments, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with mean reversion toward recent 10-day average.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment decay (e.g., 0.5% per day if sentiment <0.3).
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes; use 14-day moving average as baseline for smoothing forecast deviations.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.67), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0% to catch mean reversion trend.
